why: Keep four boundaries (top, bottom, left, right) and peel the matrix one ring at a time: walk the top row, the right column, the bottom row backwards, the left column upwards, then shrink all four.
hints: Think in rings: the outer ring first, then the same thing on the smaller inner rectangle.
Track top, bottom, left, right. After each side you walk, that boundary moves inward by one.
Loop while top <= bottom and left <= right; only walk the bottom row if top < bottom and the left column if left < right. O(rows * cols).
pitfalls: A single row or single column: without the guards you visit cells twice.
Non-square inputs like 2 x 4 leave no inner ring.
The left-column walk goes up to top + 1, not top, which is already taken.
